To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we observe a scaling of the cumulants, which can be compared to experimental results.

(1) The higher order cumulants are increasingly dominated by universal scaling laws, (2) The universal scaling laws differ from the hadron resonance model, (3) The universal scaling behavior can be used to determine the freeze out temperature in heavy ion collisions.
(i) The cumulants of baryon number and electric charge fluctuations calculated within lattice QCD show a clear scaling behavior, which allows us to relate cumulants of different orders to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of baryonic and electric charge fluctuations in QCD matter.
the investigation of the phase transition in the QCD equation of state.
the study of the QCD transition and the search for a possible critical point.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lattice QCD results are consistent with the experimental data, if the lattice results are extrapolated to the physical quark mass.
the lattice data are consistent with a first order phase transition in the QCD chiral limit.
lattice QCD calculations of higher order cumulants are in good agreement with the experimental data, and the latter are compatible with a universal scaling behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lattice data is consistent with a critical point at ( μ B, T ) ≈ ( 400 MeV, 160 MeV ).
we have obtained a set of universal ratios for the net-baryon number cumulants.
the cumulant ratios of the baryon and charge fluctuations calculated on the lattice are consistent with the hadron resonance model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the baryon number fluctuations are more sensitive to the critical point than the charge fluctuations.
lattice QCD is a powerful theoretical tool to calculate the thermodynamics of strongly interacting matter and to make quantitative predictions for the experiments.
lattice QCD calculations of higher order cumulants can provide a very useful tool to understand the nature of the QCD transition and to extract its properties.
